notes.title: April Devlog | Steady Updates, Gradual Breakthroughs
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

This month, I’ve continued pushing forward with some core content updates, along with stability improvements and polish. While the game still doesn’t have much attention, I’m committed to updating it step by step—hoping to eventually shape The Righteousness: SanGuo into a complete and enjoyable experience.

Here are the main updates for this month:

📚 New Collection Gameplay: Jianghu Anecdotes & Righteous Prosperity

This month, I’ve added two new collectible elements—an early step towards expanding the overworld map gameplay.

Jianghu Anecdotes: New interactable courier stations have been added across the world map. Players can trigger small dialogue scenes between the main cast—“the gang’s own little stories.” I hope this gives you a better sense of who these characters are. (There’s a small reward too after each one.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/a00eb4efd2d33080435138633c82139df54e4b07.jpg[/img]
Courier station where you can trigger Jianghu Anecdotes
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/b7d2d0c0d0213a5474f12a1636898b1e47a2fb28.jpg[/img]
Mini-scenes with your companions

Righteous Prosperity: Tasked by the benevolent Lord Liu Bei, the main character will help those who pose no threat—people and animals alike—across various levels, assisting in the creation of a peaceful and righteous era. These events don’t affect the main story progression, but I hope they bring a bit of warmth to your journey. Who knows, maybe they’ll even influence the game’s final ending... (Oops, light spoiler?)

I’ve always hoped The Righteousness: SanGuo would be more than just a combat game—it should carry a little “righteousness” too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/b5cc30e9613ee44d82bd9969c0dde897c981d7c9.jpg[/img]
For the people!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/c01ec8df071ee8414223548b685428d57b9b0002.jpg[/img]
Saved a 🦆

🛠 Save System Optimization

The save system has been significantly reworked, and in theory, issues like data loss or save errors should no longer occur. I’ll keep monitoring this area, and if you encounter any problems during your gameplay, please don’t hesitate to report them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/b2c1dc10eefd755070e9d016598acf74fd7b3952.jpg[/img]
Fixed in earlier patches

⚙️ Tweaks to Difficulty & Controls

I’ve made minor adjustments to the pacing of certain levels and the control logic of characters. Details were covered in previous patch notes, so I won’t repeat them here. The goal is simple: better feel, smoother flow.

🚩 Next Step: Overworld Map Arrives Earlier

Currently, the overworld map only unlocks after Chapter 4, which delays some of the more distinctive gameplay features and slows down the pacing. I’m considering moving its availability earlier—possibly right after Chapter 2—to create a smoother rhythm and let players access the “exploration and collection” elements sooner.

This direction is still being tested internally, and further changes might happen. But in any case, my priority is to make the game more rhythmic, more fun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/7daac367582126b94312e1ec87d5f8740fa173be.jpg[/img]
More explorable areas are coming
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/1d7ac2630467b29a221184d59e018aa49a5d1479.jpg[/img]
The overworld map includes a day-night cycle~

📬 A Little Closing Note (well, maybe not that little)

Although The Righteousness: SanGuo hasn’t gained much visibility yet, and sales are modest, I’ll keep working on it until it becomes a complete, engaging experience. This isn’t a short-term experiment for me—it’s a long-term creative journey.

Some might look at my journey and try to draw conclusions—"what went wrong," or use it to caution other indie devs. But did I fail? I simply never set out with the sole goal of making money.

When one person says a game is fun, you might doubt the game.
When ten people say it, you might start doubting yourself.
When a hundred say it’s fun—well, that’s the modern marketing way.

Yes, I joined a bunch of dev groups. I’ve definitely been influenced by sales rankings and success stories. But after thinking it through, I don’t really want to drag nine or ninety-nine people along to shout “The Righteousness: SanGuo is amazing! If you don’t play it, your life is less complete!”

I’d rather you keep your skepticism. Stay mentally independent.

So I’ll just say this:
“I think The Righteousness: SanGuo is pretty fun.”
And I hope we can vibe on that.

In the end, “success” or “failure” is just something we humans define for ourselves. I never intended to get rich off indie dev.

The first time I released a proper game video was when the demo was finally playable. I just genuinely love games. And I genuinely treat game development as something meaningful.

Sure, I still have a lot to learn, details to refine, and gameplay to polish... But the current version is already a big improvement over launch—it’s gone from version 7.20 to 7.23 now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/078450a979a8bc0a2d8029e587331ad05b775287.jpg[/img]
Not many people are watching, but I’m always improving the game

As a developer, sometimes I want to slack off. But as a player—I can’t stand my own laziness.
So, back to work~
(Unless a new game I love just launched… then sorry, update pause! You know how it is, haha.)

Now that The Righteousness: SanGuo is in Early Access, I honestly think that in itself is a small success (maybe shameless to say so, haha).

From starting everything alone, to gradually building the game—I created characters, environments, and props with my father in his 60s. I taught myself to develop games, and along the way received help and advice from many generous seniors.

Of course, I know luck matters. But more than anything, what I care about is:
Respecting every single person who’s willing to try my game.

Whether you've already supported it, or just stopped by to take a look—I believe you deserve genuine care.

So yeah… I think it’s all been pretty good. Pretty worth it.

If you’ve already supported this game, thank you so much—you’re one of the reasons I keep going.
If you haven’t played it yet, I hope one day you’ll be curious enough to give it a try.
Come see this little world, where I’m still seriously telling a story set in an alternate Three Kingdoms.

Finally,
I think The Righteousness: SanGuo is pretty fun.
Feel free to try it out, and I welcome your feedback and suggestions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/a4c6f0657fc63e9f73c5ae9266966574f3e3fd60.png[/img]
The Righteousness: SanGuo
Hope you have fun,
And I hope what I’ve written and made makes you feel—it was worth it.

—Dev
Carter Chang

notes.title: Action System 2.0 updated!!!
notes.content:
The Righteousness: SanGuo has been out for nearly half a month now! I'm incredibly grateful for everyone’s attention, congratulations, and for the many teachers who helped with reviews and promotions – thank you so much!

With all your support, I’m even more determined to make the game more enjoyable. That’s why I’ve given the controls and action system a major upgrade – you could call it “Action System 2.0”! Without further ado, here’s a brief introduction to what’s new in this update:

[h3]Dodge System[/h3]
Many friends mentioned that the game is too difficult, where you lose health as soon as you encounter enemies and there aren’t proper dodging mechanics. So, I’ve added a new dodge system – when dodging, your character becomes invincible for an instant, dashes a certain distance in the current direction, and leaves behind a cool afterimage effect!
However, dodging consumes stamina, and frequent use in a short period increases the consumption. Once the cooldown finishes, the consumption returns to normal, creating a balance between risk and reward.
Of course, later on, dodge performance will be further enhanced through treasures and passive upgrades, so I welcome all your feedback!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/0bd001f7709acc0fcc47e6683b30703688e7d516.gif[/img]

[h3]Charged Heavy Attack[/h3]
In response to feedback about the limited attack options, I’ve added a charged heavy attack. After charging, it not only significantly boosts your attack power but also knocks enemies back, giving you more room to survive.
Of course, charging comes with risks, so how you balance risk and reward will depend on your play.
Future passive upgrades will continue to optimize this skill’s effects.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/f990c6cb19e5772036bcda9ff8e465338bf2fd29.gif[/img]

[h3]Grappling Hook Optimization[/h3]
Simply put, the grappling hook is no longer limited by stamina.
In the third level, “Wo Long Cave”, players can acquire the grappling hook, which lets you explore more areas via hooks on the map.
Previously, the stamina cost made using the grappling hook feel cumbersome and unsatisfying. Now, you can hook as long as you want, explore freely, and have even more fun!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/fe82aa5071444b148af4cd0bfcaa44d6492708c2.gif[/img]

[h3]Feel Optimization[/h3]
Although “feel” is a somewhat abstract term, it’s vital to the gaming experience! This time, I’ve adjusted — among other things — running speed, jump height, gravity, attack intervals, landing effects, and sound effects. Playing it myself, the game feels much smoother now, and I’ve also refined some animations. I look forward to more of your feedback!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/494bede672b5894dc122a3892725067e90a6f3fd.gif[/img]

[h3]Overall Optimization[/h3]
This update features a major optimization of the main character’s code, with many redundant components removed. Additionally, there are improvements in sound effects, visual effects, and even some minor textures have been replaced. Overall, lower-end machines should theoretically run the game more smoothly. I hope these optimizations will provide a better gaming experience for everyone!

That’s all for this major upgrade to the action system. I hope you enjoy the game, and feel free to share your thoughts anytime!

Even though I’m still a novice indie game developer, I always stand on the players’ side – my main focus is listening to your feedback!

To borrow a quote from Mr. Satoru Iwata: “My business card is as a game developer, but my heart is that of a gamer!” I will continue to listen to your suggestions, so please keep them coming!

Also, with the Spring Promotion coming up soon, please come and try out The Righteousness: SanGuo then! Thank you, everyone!

Developer
Carter Chang

notes.title: The Righteousness: SanGuo is now available for Early Access!
notes.content:
Good news, everyone! It’s been a while, and I have something exciting to share with you all—

[h3] "The Righteousness: SanGuo" is now available for Early Access![/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/438e4304bddfe614a745a49e530f3c4b540d97ae.jpg[/img]
Those who follow me may know that I am not a professional game developer, but someone who, driven by a love for games, learned Unreal Engine and worked on development while designing characters with my 61-year-old father. After nearly five years of part-time development, we’ve finally reached this moment, and today TThe Righteousness: SanGuo is officially available for Early Access!

Many players may have concerns about "Early Access," fearing unstable developer mindsets or the project being abandoned halfway. I completely understand these worries, but after careful consideration, I decided to go ahead with this approach.

[h3] About the mindset [/h3]

I am not a professional game developer and don't have the "do or die" pressure; the sales of the game will not determine my survival. But this is exactly why I can approach it with a calmer mindset. I believe this freedom from market pressures will allow me to create something that is more true to my original vision.

I love games and am also just an ordinary player who sometimes wants to lie down and do nothing all afternoon. At the same time, I want to create the kind of game I enjoy, whether or not it’s a popular trend in the market. (When we first started development, Metroidvania-style games weren’t as popular as they are now, and I’m grateful for the many great predecessors who have revived this genre.) Indie games should be independent in nature—first, please yourself, then share with like-minded players. This is the balance and joy I seek.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/a62ee8d4cc3ae02464b46dd72810687c18fbd1d1.jpg[/img]
[h3] About giving up halfway [/h3]

From the very beginning, this game has been more than just a development project for me; it’s a personal commitment as a player. As a player, I want to create a game I truly love. If others like it too, that’s even better. But no matter what, I will be responsible for my work. After all, if I don’t like it, how can I expect others to?

My father and I have come a long way from initial hand-drawn sketches to a game that runs smoothly today. The process has been long, but it’s filled with satisfaction and joy. If more people can join in this joy and maybe even let me earn a little extra income, I’d be thrilled. This creation has lasted five years with no capital investment or commercialization pressure. I cherish my work and want to refine The Righteousness: SanGuo into something better and more complete. So, I won’t give up easily or let my efforts go to waste.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/27dd86814223fd8114a9ed12886f0af30cc3beea.jpg[/img]
[b]This is the confidence behind my choice to release Early Access.[/b]

[h3] About the game [/h3]

Set against the backdrop of the Three Kingdoms, players will take on the role of an amnesiac assassin, meeting historical figures from the era and weaving a unique story.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/a12aa636d48ddfaf434b7bc527204ad00bfb4697.png[/img]
The core gameplay draws inspiration from Metroidvania, offering rich, explorable environments, carefully designed enemies and boss battles, and a variety of skills to help you triumph. The game also provides a decent challenge, hoping players will find their own rhythm in the combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/2ff18962926610aee6f7dcdf1ca42b355a164c2e.jpg[/img]
In terms of art style, we aimed to provide a unique visual experience. I combined textbook illustrations from the 90s with the style of traditional Chinese comic books, leading the color palette design, attempting to recapture the feeling of scribbling in old textbooks (I’m sure many people from the 90s can relate). Character design was led by my father, as he was most familiar with the comic book style during his youth. We combined our respective experiences to craft a distinctive artistic style.

Although this is the Early Access version, about 70% of the main storyline is complete. While refining the main content, I plan to add side stories and more map exploration to further enrich the game.

[h3] About the price [/h3]

After careful consideration, the Early Access version will be priced at ¥26.

I hope this price will allow more players to experience our labor of love, while also providing support for further development. As the game content expands and optimizes, the price may adjust in the future. But in any case, I am truly grateful for the players who support us.

[h3] Lastly [/h3]

This is the current state of The Righteousness: SanGuo. I hope you all can offer valuable feedback, and I will do my best to improve it, making it a truly worthy indie game.

Please support us!

[h2] The Righteousness: SanGuo is now available for Early Access! [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/8d463886a085847d0f9e682d71837ca35b697b83.png[/img]

Thank you, everyone!

Initially, I worried that the blurriness might impact gameplay, but without texture streaming, even 64GB of RAM would quickly be maxed out. If any Unreal Engine 4/5 experts have advice, I’d greatly appreciate it!

notes.title: Develop Log Summer
notes.content:
It’s been a while since my last update at the end of April. I’ve been back to work for some time now, and though it’s tough, at least I won’t starve, so the game development continues. I’ve returned to my previous routine of developing the game after work in the evenings. Progress is slow, but I’ve managed to accomplish quite a bit. Here’s a brief update on what I’ve been working on these past few months.

[h3]Development and Improvement of the Dialogue System:[/h3]

The dialogue system is now complete and can be used in any scene. Previously, I didn’t optimize this feature, which resulted in characters standing still during conversations. Now that the system is improved, I have more time to design character positions, camera angles, and cutscenes. However, some of the previously created static dialogues are too complex to modify all at once. I’ll address these through updates, and I hope you understand.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/de37154f9f3ea580740a9fcba2644f4cd97ff88c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/3d1e62b35c2b51595f8d2dfac8fb36179312c3c8.png[/img]

[h3]Boss Battle Optimization:[/h3]

The game’s boss battles aren’t limited to humanoid bosses; there are also levels involving auxiliary equipment. I’ve optimized some of the previously created boss battles and made adjustments to new ones.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/0cea2f86580af990885e5a4cd75f42a70c24a05c.png[/img]


[h3]Level Data:[/h3]

With the dialogue system complete, it naturally needs to integrate with the previously created levels. Over the past few months, I’ve been connecting levels, modifying announcements, cutscenes, and determining the data needed for storage and retrieval in each level. There might be some missing data… I can only ask that you don’t be too harsh if you encounter issues and please provide feedback so I can fix them promptly.


[h3]Performance Adjustments:[/h3]

I’ve optimized many assets and logic (mostly issues left from my early self-learning days without practical experience). The game now runs at a stable 60 FPS on my home laptop with a 1050ti, and at a smooth 120 FPS on my desktop with a 4070ti.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/5d6192679daa5f49d0b95075707b4c6cde776e32.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/d42a86c94a590c0ea615cb80491fc1fd613a9e0a.jpg[/img]

[h3]Packaging and Testing:[/h3]

I’ve conducted packaging tests, and the game runs well. The game size is around 7GB, and the optimization is decent. I’m also testing the packaged version for bugs and continuously making improvements.

That’s what I’ve been busy with lately. The main focus has been on connecting levels and chapters, which has brought up many unforeseen issues. So, it’s been a lot of bug fixing along the way. I haven’t been able to write logs mainly because work has been exhausting lately… After developing the game at home, I just don’t feel like writing. Hello everyone, it has been two months since I announced in October that I would temporarily work full-time on developing Three Kingdoms Anytime. First of all, I didn’t post a monthly report in November not because the game was cancelled, but because I was working on the character and animation materials that took a lot of time. I didn’t do any other work besides that, so I decided not to post a November report and focus on development work. Next is the official monthly report.

[h3]November:[/h3] 
I spent the whole month dealing with art materials. [b]Art:[/b] Fortunately, by the end of November, I had processed 95% of the materials. Because some of the level mechanisms were not fully implemented, I left some materials unmade for the time being. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/74fb11f89364fbd03c084b70d3a417cb399c0c56.jpg[/img] 

[b]Programming:[/b] 
After completing the character materials, I also implemented them in the game and optimized the AI logic. The preparatory work for the miscellaneous soldiers is basically completed. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/bc1f08352aee41ce249da7cf4f80e863a3763ee2.jpg[/img] I’m quite relieved to see so many materials processed. [h3]December:[/h3] I officially entered the important level polishing work, and I have completed almost 4 chapters of content, and I’m still continuing. 

[b]Art:[/b] 
This month, I started to polish each level again, as usual, breaking down the large levels into smaller ones that load faster, improving the game experience, and checking and modifying the materials that cause performance problems. After saying so much, it’s actually for the sake of frame rate. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/ee5e8d6450c98c460e0e0fe0463c8b9ff1bea483.jpg[/img] 
You can see that the game frame rate is currently stable at 120FPS on the development machine, and it can also reach a relatively stable 60FPS on my 1050ti laptop.

During this period, I also revised the early character animations. I don’t say that I reached any standard, but at least it’s a small improvement for myself. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42182567/64fec125def021eec13b4124f17b559928505b46.gif[/img]

[b]Programming:[/b]
I mainly improved the skills of the characters, because there are many things in terms of gameplay, the initial design and the final implementation are still some differences, and they need to be adjusted in continuous testing. At the same time, in the process of independent development, it is also a continuous learning process. For the “perfect” logic that I wrote before, it always looks awkward, so I also improved and optimized them one by one. Then there is the storage function, although it was done early, but to make a game with some RPG characteristics, the storage of various data is more cumbersome, I am still simplifying and improving.

[h3]Summary:[/h3]
Organize art resources, improve level design, and ensure the game is developed steadily.

[i]Finally, let me talk about something else,[/i]
Overall, these two months of full-time development time was very ample. To be honest, working for myself is really happy, at least I don’t have to be angry at work, and overtime is actually creating some substantive things, but after full-time independent development, the income is basically zero, I honestly say this point is definitely not happy, but thanks to the understanding of family and friends’ encouragement, I can stick to it, I will continue to develop steadily, and strive to launch the game as soon as possible, let everyone experience the story of Three Kingdoms Renyi Chuan. notes.title: The DEMO of " The Righteousness: SanGuo " is coming!

[b]Performance[/b]

Enemy frame optimization,
Because before the game development experience, so the use of violence invoked a lot of data, resulting in a decline in performance, in the months before the enemy significantly optimize the overall framework, namely enemy framework version 2.0, this version of the framework, AI logic more unobstructed, later period maintenance more convenient also.

Scene collision optimization,
In the same way that the previous scenario used violent calls to the collision result to handle the collision, it now uses fewer calls to achieve the same effect.

[b]Control[/b]
Increased the jumping power of the main character, now players can jump higher, easier to board the platform.
The hook system is optimized.
Increased the movement speed of the main character.
Added the ability to use gamepads to control the UI.

[b]Visual[/b]
The biggest change is the unification of the fonts. Last time playtest used simplified Chinese and traditional Chinese. Later, some friends reported that it looked very confusing.
Shadow effects have removed the overlap of wrong lighting.
The tone has also been retuned.
Improved the gallery system.
As one of the more important functions of the game, the gallery system has completed the v1 version and will continue to improve and expand.

In terms of scene construction, character animation has been completed this month with two large BOSS characters and two BOSS station scene mechanisms, so I won't go into details here.
